title: HSA strategy chain
description:
A chain / composition definition (PID lines 57-82). A chain is the separate composition model that combines normalised atomic outputs; the atomic strategies themselves stay unaware of each other.

CANONICAL PRIMITIVES are exactly ALL, ANY, SEQUENCE, CONTEXT_TRIGGER (PID lines 65-68). The enum is closed: a new primitive is a PID change, not a document change.

NO CHAIN-OF-CHAIN RECURSION — deliberate structural restriction: PID line 82 says prefer atomic-strategy inputs to chains in v1, and do not create recursive chain-of-chain complexity unless explicitly authorised. This schema makes that impossible rather than discouraged. A chain is FLAT by construction: it declares exactly one primitive at the top level and an inputs array whose items are atomic strategy references only. There is no reusable node definition, no self $ref, and no chain_id / chain_version / sub_chain property anywhere inside inputs. Combined with additionalProperties false on the input item, a nested object carrying its own primitive and inputs is rejected, and so is a reference to another chain document. Consequences accepted on purpose: an expression such as ALL of (context, ANY of (trigger_a, trigger_b)) cannot be expressed in v1 and must be split into separately governed chains. Both PID acceptance examples (lines 234-242) are flat and fit this model. Relaxing the restriction later is additive — permitting a nested node as an alternative inputs item would not invalidate any document written against this version — whereas allowing recursion now and withdrawing it later would break every document that used it.

IDENTITY PRESERVATION: inputs reference atomic strategies by strategy_id plus strategy_version together (PID line 72). Version is required, never implied, so a chain always pins the exact immutable atomic version it was proven against (PID lines 185-189).

primitive.description: The single composition primitive this chain applies to its inputs. ALL: every input must match. ANY: at least one input must match. SEQUENCE: inputs must match in ascending sequence_index order within the declared window. CONTEXT_TRIGGER: a higher-timeframe CONTEXT input must hold while a lower-timeframe TRIGGER input fires.

inputs.description: Atomic strategy references only. See the chain-of-chain note in this schema's top-level description for why nothing else is permitted here.

timeframe_roles.description: Semantic role to concrete timeframe mapping (PID lines 84-97). Role names are canonical; the timeframes they map to are a per-strategy choice, so 4H/1H/15M/5M and 1D/4H/1H/15M are both legal. This is a hypothesis structure, not a guarantee of edge (PID line 97).

state_semantics.description: State the chain carries between evaluations (PID lines 73, 138). A chain that latches a context or an armed trigger must say so explicitly.

timing.description: When the chain is evaluated and, for SEQUENCE, the window inside which the ordered steps must complete (PID lines 75, 137).

persistence.description: How long a match remains asserted once produced (PID lines 76, 137).

expiry.description: When an un-consumed match or a latched state goes stale (PID lines 77, 137). If expires is true, the bar count and its timeframe are mandatory: an expiry without a measurable horizon is exactly the kind of discretionary language HSA must refuse (PID lines 110-120).

explanation_contract.description: PID line 80 requires an explicit reason for match AND for non-match. Those three flags are const true, so no chain can be authored that reports a bare boolean. A non-match with no reason is unauditable and therefore not governable.

per_input_evaluation_reported.description: The reason must attribute the outcome to individual inputs, using each atomic strategy's own reason_field.

composition_assertions.description: Machine-checkable restatement of PID lines 59, 72 and 82.

atomic_input.description: A reference to one atomic strategy, by identity and version together. This is the ONLY thing a chain may compose. It carries no primitive and no nested inputs, which is what makes chain-of-chain recursion structurally unreachable rather than merely discouraged.

input_id.description: Local handle for this input, used by the explanation contract to attribute a match or non-match. Must be unique within the chain; uniqueness across inputs is a semantic check, not expressible in JSON Schema.

strategy_version.description: Required, never inferred. Pinning the exact version is how component identity survives composition (PID line 72).

direction.description: INHERIT takes the chain's resolved direction; EITHER matches regardless of the input's own direction.

sequence_index.description: 1-based position. Required when the chain primitive is SEQUENCE, meaningless otherwise.

optional.description: An optional step, as in the optional lower-timeframe trigger of PID line 242. An optional input can never be the sole cause of a match.
